news.title: The mystery of sub-Neptunes – the planets we thought shouldn’t exist
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print Christian Gralingen For almost a decade, the Kepler Space Telescope trailed Earth’s orbit, watching out for flickers in the light of distant stars.

In 2011, two years after its launch, the NASA mission found what it was looking for: the signature of a roughly Earth-sized planet dimming out a tiny sliver of light as it transited across the face of its star. The identification of Kepler-10b, a planet almost 1.5 times the size of Earth that orbits a star around 600 light years away, was the first time we had spotted a rocky exoplanet – a world beyond our solar system.

Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. news.title: Where Does Language Originate in the Brain? New Research Challenges Our 150-Year-Old Understanding
paras: That’s because in the 1870s, German neurologist Carl Wernicke noticed that people with damage to that area struggled to comprehend words. Speech production, on the other hand, was believed to stem from a separate place called Broca’s area, near the left temple.

However, individuals with damage to Wernicke’s area sometimes also spoke in fluent-sounding gibberish, talking in what’s described as “word salad,” perplexing researchers. Now, one team may have figured out why: Wernicke’s area actually pulls double duty, helping both process speech and produce it. The findings, published in the journal Science on November 19, rewrite our understanding of how the brain constructs language and can help scientists develop technologies that restore speech.

news.title: Biologists Discover a 'One-in-a-Million' Bright Yellow Burbot Fish in New York's Oswego Harbor
paras: Add as preferred source The rare fish, whose species is native to the Great Lakes, was discovered during an invasive species survey. Fish and Wildlife Service Burbots typically blend into their surroundings with a mottled palette of olive green, earthy brown and golden yellow.

So when biologists pulled a bright yellow fish from New York’s Oswego Harbor, they knew they had caught something unusual. The burbot had a rare biological condition called xanthochromism, which produces an unusually saturated yellow or orange hue in otherwise normally colored animals. It results from a genetic mutation that reduces the production of black-brown melanin, which allows yellow pigment to dominate.
